title: Staged hiring + price-bands sensitivity matrix
summary: Working draft: combine multi-horizon headcount phasing with three price-band strategies to surface revenue and margin sensitivity. Purpose is to inform FY26-FY28 hiring cadence and potential discounting/commit tiers for Dedicated contracts. Not final — needs SRE and product validation on delivery timelines for Dedicated capacity features.
assumptions:
- Base revenue growth (no price change) = 65% YoY for hosted API in FY26, then 35% FY27, 20% FY28.
- Dedicated adoption increases ARR by onboarding 8 mid-market customers in FY26, 20 in FY27, 35 in FY28 (aggressive).
- Average Dedicated contract size = $120k ARR at list price band A.
- Staffing ramp: hiring phased across engineering, SRE, sales, solutions eng, and finance. Average fully-burdened cost per hire = $220k/year for engineering; $150k/year for GTM roles.
- Pricing bands: A (list), B (10% discount), C (20% discount + longer commit).
- Elasticity: estimated uplift in conversion for Dedicated when moving from A->B = +30% conversion; A->C = +65%. These are directional and should be stress-tested.
- Unit cost per token reduced by quantization/optimizations over time: -12% in FY26, -8% in FY27.
- Cache/batching improvements assumed to reduce variable GPU spend vs revenue by 8% in first year of deployment for dedicated workloads.
headcount_phasing:
High-level sequencing (working numbers):
- Q3 2025: finalize FY26 hiring plan; freeze non-critical projects.
- Q4 2025: hire 6 infra/SRE (to support Dedicated private deployments), 4 serving-runtime engineers (latency and batching), 3 solutions engineers for early Dedicated pilots.
- Q1 2026: ramp GTM: 6 AE/AMs + 4 pre-sales SEs; hire 8 cloud ops/infra; staggered to align with Dedicated GA.
- FY26 total target: 46 net hires (22 eng, 14 GTM, rest finance/ops).
- FY27: expand to 60–80 net hires depending on revenue trajectory; emphasize product and SRE for multi-region.
Notes: hiring cadence tied to committed revenue milestones; delay of Dedicated GA by >=2 quarters pushes ~30% of FY26 hiring into FY27.
pricing_sensitivity_analysis:
Three levers modeled: price band, conversion uplift, and committed term length.
Key findings (draft):
- Moving from A -> B (10% discount) increases Dedicated conversion by ~30% in model; increases gross new ARR but compresses margins enough that near-term EBITDA benefit is mixed (depends on CAC amortization period).
- Moving from A -> C (20% discount + 2yr minimum) can materially grow pipeline (modeled +65%), but reduces first-year margin by ~4–6 percentage points in base case; longer-term NPV is positive if churn remains <6%/yr.
- If we can pair B/C with faster onboarding (reduce time-to-first-dollar by 25%), the margin compression is partially offset due to shorter CAC payback. That requires +4 pre-sales hires concurrent with contract offers.
- Sensitivity heatmap highlights a fragile zone: price band C + delayed onboarding = margin breach below target (EBITDA margin <10%) under conservative revenue growth.
Recommendations in this sheet consider staged discounts where deeper discounts require commitments to minimum onboarding SLAs and tooling investments (onboarding automation budget ~$450k one-time).
recommended_actions:
1) Keep list price (A) as gating baseline; pilot B in two sales plays: mid-market retail and regulated verticals with 6-month commits.
2) Only enable C (20%/2yr) if customer signs onboarding SLA and pays 50% upfront or we deploy Dedicated into a 'reserved pool' that can be shared across 2 customers for multi-tenant periods.
3) Defer 40% of FY26 non-essential brand/product roles to FY27 unless pipeline hits committed ARR milestones: $6M ARR from Dedicated by end of Q1 FY26.
4) Allocate $450k one-time for onboarding automation (engineering + small solutions team) to shorten time-to-first-dollar; model shows payback in 9–12 months given base case conversion uplift.
5) Re-run sensitivity model monthly with updated conversion metrics from sales pilots; freeze new hires if conversion < baseline for two consecutive months.
open_questions:
- Are the conversion uplift assumptions (30%/65%) defensible? Need Sales & Solutions empirical input from pilots.
- Is $120k ARR avg Dedicated contract realistic — Ops has seen variance ±40% by sector. Update with pipeline by sector.
- Impact of quantization and model optimizations on unit cost is sticky — Research to provide updated guidance by Nov 2025.
- Should we consider an intermediate price band (A-.05) tied to 12-month commits to smooth elasticity? Quick test needed.
- Legal: standard T&Cs for two-year committed discounts (C) — what are escalation/exit clauses; ops risk?
